Audi’s Upcoming 2028 RS6 Avant Gets a Virtual Tuning Job
12 photos
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project
It’s been one a half years since production of the all-new sixth-generation Audi A6 kicked off, yet there is still no RS 6 in the company’s lineup. However, that’s about to change, as the four-ring brand’s Sport division is putting the final touches on the range-topping version of the series.
Unlike its predecessors, which were only available as five-door station wagons, the all-new RS 6 will be offered in two body styles. The four-door sedan will join the Avant for the first time since the C6. The latter model was launched at the Frankfurt Motor Show back in 2007, with production starting that same year and ending in 2011. It was based on the same nuts and bolts as the era’s A6, as well as the S6 and A6 allroad quattro.
As for the all-new Audi RS 6 , it will utilize the PPC (Premium Platform Combustion) bones. Thus, it will have a lot of things in common not only with the lesser A6 family, but also the smaller A5 (B10), the latest Q5, the new-generation Q7, and the first-ever Q9. The construction is therefore on the versatile side of things, as it can accommodate plenty of models, from premium compact vehicles to full-size SUVs.
It is yet unknown when the upcoming RS 6 will go official, as Audi has yet to announce the unveiling date, though from what we can tell, we are probably months away (or is that weeks?) from seeing it under the spotlight, with no camouflage on its body. Chances are it will probably arrive at dealers across the United States of America for the 2028 model year, and the automaker is expected to offer it in both body styles (Sedan and Avant).
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project Now, if the official unveiling of the all-new Audi RS 6 hasn’t taken place yet, then how has this model been visited by the tuning fairy? Well, it’s a virtual visit, as mentioned in the title. The renderings came from @ildar_project on Instagram, and they portray the model with a more aggressive body kit. Chances are we will eventually see some similar builds once the model goes official, as numerous tuners will offer all kinds of upgrades for it.
For now, this CGI-tuned new-gen Audi RS 6 Avant sports an entirely new hood that is on the vented side of things. The large splitter with blades on the sides is also new, and there are some add-ons surrounding the vents on each side of the grille, as well as yellow daytime running lights, which are part of the virtual makeover. The door mirror casings have also come from the CGI tuning game, just like the side skirts.
The wheel arches appear to be a bit wider than on the stock car, and further back, this imagined Audi RS 6 Avant has a pair of spoilers above and below the rear windscreen. There is also a new diffuser with a motorsport-like extra brake light in the middle, as well as cutouts for the RS signature dual oval tailpipes. The car sits closer to the ground than usual, rides on large concave wheels with a Y-spoke design, and has a satin green look on the outside, as well as some forged carbon accents.
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project The usual RS logos decorate its exterior, which also sports some black details for more contrast, and while the interior hasn’t opened up in these digital illustrations, we already know what we are looking at, because it will be virtually identical to that of the new-gen A6. Well, save for the front bucket seats, the dedicated load screens and submenus on the displays, the steering wheel, trim and upholstery, and some other bits and bobs, as these will draw a clear line between the A6 and the RS 6.
Moreover, a reworked chassis setup will also be part of the real RS makeover, alongside a set of beefier brakes. The latter are a must in order to keep the power in check. Previous information claimed that the new RS 6 might get the plug-in hybrid V8 assembly from the Bentley Continental GT Speed, which is officially good for 771 hp (782 ps/575 kW).
However, new data suggests that we might be looking at a V6 with electric assistance, and it could be the same setup used on the new RS 5 . This model has a twin-turbo 2.9-liter V6 mill that is good for 503 hp (510 ps/375 kW), and the electric motor is rated at 174 hp (177 ps/130 kW). The total output stands at 630 hp (639 ps/470 kW), enabling 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) in 3.6 seconds. The RS 5 has a roughly 50-mile (80 km) electric driving range with the 22 kWh battery pack fully charged.
Audi’s upcoming RS 6 will likely offer more oomph, and the rumor mill speaks about 740 hp (750 ps/552 kW ) or so in total. Guess we will find out if that’s true when the model premieres. But if you had to choose between the next-gen RS 6 and the current BMW M5, which one would you get and why? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ильдар (@ildar_project)
